pull_requests.title: Connect Praxis to the independently maintained Praxis SDK
pull_requests.body:
## Why
Praxis currently resolves OpenHands SDK and Automation releases and offers an implicit hosted cloud destination. This migration switches runtime dependencies to sources controlled by Praxiss-Lab.

## Summary
- Pin all four SDK packages to `Praxiss-Lab/praxis-sdk@30e562b050cddb2deb651b06168cefd35b4fb9c2`, including Automation's SDK environment.
- Bundle an adapted Automation 1.19.3 source snapshot and controlled TypeScript client 1.54.0/extensions 0.29.0 archives; lock npm dependencies to those files. Preserve original licenses and attribution.
- Build Docker's base from the pinned SDK source and include Automation in desktop packaging.
- Require an explicit compatible cloud host before login and point deployment help to the owned documentation. Update runtime/development guides.

## Verification
VERIFIED: 152 launcher/version-check tests and 50 backend/device-flow/settings tests passed. Typecheck, web build, targeted ESLint (warnings only), formatting, version sync and repository static checks passed. Source-backed Agent Server `/server_info` and bundled Automation `/health` returned HTTP 200. npm archive contents include Automation and both SDK client/extensions dependencies. Companion SDK validation passed 705 targeted Python tests and 383 TypeScript tests.
VERIFIED IN CI: Docker image build and complete/split mode smoke checks passed at commit `358f5f467e0247b2b988b4d444bd2f6e61c19acd`; Linux, Windows and macOS desktop packaging passed. Companion SDK passed all eight Actions workflows.
UNKNOWN: manual installed Electron execution was not run in this environment.

## CI corrections
Docker now inherits the SDK image's Debian repositories, avoiding incompatible library/header snapshots. Hosted integration links require `VITE_PRODUCT_URL` and otherwise open deployment guidance. Update stale documentation, image and explicit-host test expectations.

Current local validation: all 8,398 Praxis unit tests passed (7 todo); 232 focused migration tests, typecheck, full lint (warnings only), app/library builds, formatting and SDK version sync passed. Mock analytics handlers now intercept all PostHog regions and paths, and Docker mode checks suppress frontend telemetry at runtime. 106 analytics/static-server regression tests passed without external analytics transport. All seven GitHub Actions workflows passed at commit `358f5f467e0247b2b988b4d444bd2f6e61c19acd`, including full core verification, Docker complete/split mode checks, and desktop packaging for Linux, Windows and macOS.

## Upstream provenance
ADAPT: SDK baseline `c4b93299cf2b31c8b5d0b2c5a89965ccc5ff24f9`, Automation 1.19.3 sdist and extensions 0.29.0. Praxis-original source selection, deployment wiring and documentation. Snapshot checksums are documented in `vendor/README.md`.

## Risk / compatibility impact
Python import names, npm package names and OH_* variables remain compatibility identifiers. SDK/client versions move from 1.53.0 to 1.54.0 and bundled Automation from 1.19.0 to 1.19.3. Explicitly configured legacy cloud integrations and saved endpoints remain available; no hosted Praxis cloud is provisioned. Owned image defaults require independently built/published images. No automatic upstream SDK/Automation package fallback remains.

## Documentation impact
Added `docs/SDK_INDEPENDENCE.md` and snapshot provenance. Updated README, Windows/development docs and local runtime/desktop guidance.

## Type
- [x] Docs / chore
- [x] Upstream integration

## Known limitations / follow-ups
Companion SDK PR: https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/praxis-sdk/pull/1. These branches are not merged. Repository visibility remains unchanged. Manual installed Electron verification remains required before release.

pull_requests.title: fix: restore parallel native release runners [skip ci]
pull_requests.body:
Release image builds currently run amd64 and emulated arm64 on one runner. Restore the upstream native-runner approach: parallel ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm jobs, separate BuildKit cache scopes, and a dependent job publishing one multiarch version tag from this run's exact digest artifacts.

📄 [Design doc](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/Emilio-01-T/Praxis/blob/eac6f2f083d9f61199a12a8ec6fc1c4528f5cdfe/.pr/design.html)

Manual-only release dispatch, verified source commit/version, full prepublication tests, three Docker launch modes, stable-only latest, provenance and SBOM remain supported. No architecture tags or separate package names are created. The manifest helper validates each source architecture, combines both digests, checks preserved child manifests/attestations, and exposes the final index digest to GitHub Release creation.

Validation: 11 tests in 3 targeted suites passed, including stable/prerelease tagging, refusal to publish with missing/wrong-architecture inputs, and failure on lost attestations. Node syntax, workflow YAML/job dependencies, repository static checks, targeted ESLint and diff checks passed. Docker/native runner execution is not available in the local workspace; the next dispatched release will validate the complete native build and registry flow. No workflow rerun or image republishing is triggered by this change.

The existing 1.25.0 release completed successfully on its original source. This change applies to future releases.

pull_requests.title: Release-only images and split Docker launch modes
pull_requests.body:
Praxis publishes GHCR images only through the manually dispatched release, and adds frontend-only/backend-only modes to the existing image while preserving native OpenHands launcher flags.

📄 [Design doc](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/Emilio-01-T/Praxis/blob/ad378067571034c4240a952085ad47c303361ec7/.pr/design.html)

Backend mode includes Agent Server and Automation with API ingress. Frontend mode serves Canvas and optionally proxies an independent backend, including WebSockets and the editor, without embedding backend credentials. Includes split Compose examples and distribution/release documentation.

Release verification pins the dispatched commit and version, builds native artifacts, tests Docker modes, directly calls reusable image publication, and creates the GitHub release with a native archive and image digest. PR/main checks build local images only: no PR/SHA/architecture image tags. Stable releases also update latest. Publication is sequential, so a release-creation failure may leave its image already published.

Local validation: 74 targeted tests; foundation, typecheck, lint (existing warnings), shell/Node/YAML syntax and app/library builds passed. Native archive includes launcher, built app and config. Additional ingress, static-server, SDK-version and runtime-metadata suites also pass. Docker Check now records connecting Canvas to a real Agent Server (1.53.0) through the split frontend proxy; no model execution is involved. Docker Check passed on b8b268e6a081880c4b7350ad88715fbd2251e841: complete/backend/frontend modes, browser authentication, automation routes, runtime metadata and backend restart. Core CI passed on the same commit: 789 test files, 8,368 passed tests (7 todo), app/library builds and package verification.

[Real Docker browser screenshots and videos](https://github.com/Emilio-01-T/Praxis/actions/runs/37506181685/artifacts/11431792198). Backend: real Agent Server 1.53.0 and Automation 1.19.0; no LLM/model execution. The recording adds the backend through Canvas onboarding, verifies browser API authentication and captures the running app.

The final follow-up separates lint from typecheck, avoiding a repeated TypeScript check in CI and release verification. Local lint validation covers this script-only change; its commit and the squash merge use [skip ci] at the user's request, so the full suite applies to the preceding runtime implementation.

The temporary design document has been removed from the final tree; its commit-pinned link remains available.

pull_requests.title: chore: bootstrap Praxis fork foundation
pull_requests.body:
## Why

Praxis needs an independently controlled foundation before structural product development begins. The fork inherited OpenHands CI, release, package-publishing, issue-bot, and cross-repository automation that is not automatically valid for an independent repository.

## Summary

- recorded the exact OpenHands upstream baseline;
- preserved MIT licensing and added Praxis attribution;
- defined independent Praxis versioning, engineering, release, and upstream-integration policies;
- audited inherited GitHub Actions and isolated OpenHands-specific write/publish workflows;
- added Praxis-owned CI and Foundation invariant checks;
- redirected container publication/default image identity to `ghcr.io/emilio-01-t/praxis`;
- added upstream fetch/report tooling;
- documented deployment, rollback, branding/compatibility, and the Foundation Gate;
- replaced the inherited PR template with a Praxis-specific contribution contract.

## Verification

Current evidence is tracked in `docs/foundation/FOUNDATION_GATE.md`.

The automatic Praxis CI and Docker/GHCR pipeline are still being verified on this branch. Transitional failures from inherited `pull_request_target` workflows are documented in `docs/foundation/ACTION_MIGRATION_LOG.md`; those workflows execute from the current base branch and cannot be disabled for this same PR by changing their definitions only on the PR branch.

## Upstream provenance

Baseline: `OpenHands/OpenHands@81e83760a196ba6374ad2c3d38d577262c79ca2d`.

This PR is primarily Praxis-original Foundation/governance work layered onto that baseline.

## Risk / compatibility impact

- no product-domain architecture redesign is included;
- internal OpenHands identifiers are intentionally retained where renaming would increase upstream integration cost;
- publishing/release workflows with OpenHands organization authority are disabled;
- Docker publication is moved to the Praxis GHCR namespace;
- deployment to the existing VM is not yet performed by this PR.

## Documentation impact

Foundation documentation has been added under `docs/foundation/`, `docs/policies/`, and `docs/upstream/`.

## Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Docs / chore
- [ ] Upstream integration

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- Praxis CI must complete successfully;
- GHCR container build/publish must be verified;
- Praxis-specific runtime smoke tests are still pending;
- target VM deployment and rollback evidence are pending;
- repository main-protection rules must be configured after final required check names stabilize.

releases.name: Praxis 1.25.0
releases.body:
## Install Praxis 1.25.0

Choose Docker or a native installation. Both support complete, backend-only and frontend-only modes. The backend includes Agent Server and Automation.

### Docker: download and start

Install Docker Engine on Linux, or Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows (with WSL 2 integration on Windows). The image supports Linux `amd64` and `arm64`; Docker selects the matching architecture.

To download only the image, use this direct command:

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/praxiss-lab/praxis:1.25.0
```

To download and start the complete application, use:

```sh
export PRAXIS_IMAGE="ghcr.io/praxiss-lab/praxis:1.25.0"
docker pull "$PRAXIS_IMAGE"
docker run -it --rm --name praxis \
  -p 127.0.0.1:18080:8000 \
  -e PRAXIS_MODE=all \
  -e AGENT_CANVAS_ALLOW_LAN_SESSION_KEY=true \
  -v praxis-state:/home/openhands/.openhands \
  -v praxis-projects:/projects \
  "$PRAXIS_IMAGE"
```

Open **http://127.0.0.1:18080/canvas/** and configure your model provider in the UI. On Linux, prefix Docker commands with `sudo` if your Docker installation requires it.

`Ctrl+C` stops this container. The named volumes keep conversations, settings and projects; rerun the same command to start again. To use an existing host project directory, replace `-v praxis-projects:/projects` with `-v /absolute/path/to/projects:/projects`. Choose only directories you intend the agent to access.

In another terminal, check the backend:

```sh
curl --fail --show-error --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:18080/health
```

A healthy backend responds with `{"status":"ok"}`. A successful health request alone does not verify model execution.

### Backend on a server or personal VM

Use the same versioned image on the server. Generate a session key once and retain it for subsequent starts:

```sh
export PRAXIS_IMAGE="ghcr.io/praxiss-lab/praxis:1.25.0"
export PRAXIS_SESSION_API_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
docker pull "$PRAXIS_IMAGE"
docker run -d --name praxis-backend --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
  -e PRAXIS_MODE=backend \
  -e OH_SESSION_API_KEYS_0="$PRAXIS_SESSION_API_KEY" \
  -v praxis-state:/home/openhands/.openhands \
  -v praxis-projects:/projects \
  "$PRAXIS_IMAGE"
```

This binds only to the server's loopback interface. Put an HTTPS reverse proxy or private-network tunnel in front of it as described in the [self-hosting guide](https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/blob/v1.25.0/docs/SELF_HOSTING.md). Backend mode serves the APIs and Automation; it does not serve `/canvas/`.

On your frontend device:

```sh
export PRAXIS_IMAGE="ghcr.io/praxiss-lab/praxis:1.25.0"
docker pull "$PRAXIS_IMAGE"
docker run -it --rm --name praxis-frontend \
  -p 127.0.0.1:18080:8000 \
  -e PRAXIS_MODE=frontend \
  -e PRAXIS_BACKEND_URL=https://backend.example.com \
  "$PRAXIS_IMAGE"
```

Replace `https://backend.example.com` with your backend origin, reachable from the frontend container. Open **http://127.0.0.1:18080/canvas/** and enter the backend session key when requested. Without `PRAXIS_BACKEND_URL`, use the UI backend selector; direct connections require browser reachability and allowed-origin configuration.

For two containers on one machine, see the [split Compose instructions](https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/blob/v1.25.0/docs/distribution/README.md#separate-containers-on-one-machine). All modes download the same image and select which services to start. Each personal VM has independent state and credentials.

### Native installation without Docker

Install **Node.js 24+**, npm, and **uv/uvx** first. On Windows, run these commands inside WSL 2. Download the archive attached to this release:

```sh
curl --fail --location --output praxis-1.25.0.tgz \
  https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/releases/download/v1.25.0/openhands-agent-canvas-1.25.0.tgz
npm install -g ./praxis-1.25.0.tgz
agent-canvas
```

Open **http://localhost:8000/canvas/**. Native agent execution can access the host filesystem: choose the intended workspace. If npm's global installation directory is not writable, configure a user-owned npm prefix.

For separate native processes, run `agent-canvas --backend-only` on the backend host and `agent-canvas --frontend-only` on the frontend host. Use separate ports if both run on one machine; see the [distribution guide](https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/blob/v1.25.0/docs/distribution/README.md). The archive filename and `agent-canvas` command are retained technical identifiers; this archive is distributed by Praxis.

### Artifacts and troubleshooting

- **Docker image:** `ghcr.io/praxiss-lab/praxis:1.25.0`.
- **Native archive:** `openhands-agent-canvas-1.25.0.tgz`, attached under Assets.
- **image.txt:** records the build's source commit and published image digest.
- This pipeline does not attach desktop installers. Native installation above starts the web application.
- If Docker returns `unauthorized`, the package owner must check that the organization permits public packages and that this package's visibility is **Public**. A public repository alone does not make its package public.
- If port 18080 is occupied, change only the host side of the port mapping and open that port in your browser.
- For startup errors, inspect the foreground output or run `docker logs praxis-backend` for the detached backend.

See the [versioned README](https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/blob/v1.25.0/README.md), [distribution guide](https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/blob/v1.25.0/docs/distribution/README.md), and [Windows instructions](https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/blob/v1.25.0/README.windows.md).

## What's Changed

### Maintenance

* chore: bootstrap Praxis fork foundation by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/2

### Other Changes

* chore: record Praxis post-merge foundation verification by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/3
* chore: add Praxis runtime deployment gate by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/4
* chore: prepare Praxis target VM deployment verification by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/5
* docs: close Praxis Fork Foundation after local verification by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/6
* Release-only images and split Docker launch modes by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/7
* chore: prepare initial Praxis 1.25.0 release [skip ci] by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/8
* docs: remove internal planning from public documentation [skip ci] by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/9
* fix: restore parallel native release runners [skip ci] by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/10
* docs: clarify Praxis installation and launch modes [skip ci] by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/11
* docs: present Praxis and independent personal clouds by @Emilio-01-T in https://github.com/Praxiss-Lab/Praxis/pull/12

## New Contributors
